newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-HUSSAIN HITS TEST-BEST 207 IN RECORD STAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HUSSAIN HITS TEST-BEST 207 IN RECORD STAND.

text.p: Nasser Hussain stroked his test-best of 207 and shared in a record stand to tighten England's grip on the opening Ashes clash against Australia on Friday.
Hussain and Thorpe, who also made his highest test score with 138, added 288 for the fourth wicket to power England to 449 for six when rain forced an early close on the second day of the first test.
England lead by 331 after skittling Australia for 118 in their first innings.

Resuming at 200 for three, both Hussain and Thorpe batted superbly to set their fourth-wicket record for England against Australia, beating the 222 by Wally Hammong and Eddie Paynter at Lord's in 1938.

Hussain was at the crease for seven hours 20 minutes, facing 336 balls and hitting 38 fours. Thorpe took 19 fours from 245 balls before pulling Glenn McGrath from outside off-stump to give Michael Bevan an easy catch at mid-on.
Hussain finally edged a catch to the wicket off Shane Warne, who failed otherwise to make any impression.
That was as disconcerting as anything for the Australian captain Mark Taylor, who will come under even more pressure to resign if he fails again with the bat and England win the match.
Left short of bowlers by injuries to Jason Gillespie and Greg Blewett, he caused a surprise by failing to bring on paceman Mike Kasprowicz until the second new ball was taken shortly before lunch.
Kasprowicz was the best of the bowlers thereafter, richly deserving the wicket of John Crawley for only one soon after Thorpe's departure.
But Kent all-rounder Alan Ealham (32 not out) and Glamorgan's Robert Croft (18 not out) prevented any possibility of a collapse.

England's big total also removed any worry about test matches being taken away from Edgbaston after low-scoring tests in the previous two years had led to a warning from the English cricket authorities that the standard of pitch needed to improve.
Australian coach Geoff Marsh confirmed that he had requested that an additional bowler be sent to join the tour party.
"We've spoken to the selectors and put a few names up," he said. "Now it's up to them who they pick."
Fast bowlers Paul Reiffel and Adam Dale were the two players Marsh had previously mentioned as contenders.
The weather forecast for both Saturday and Sunday was for showers, some of them heavy, which gave greater encouragement to the beleaguered Australians.
